summary: 0.8.7 W7, the window wiring. (1) Her voice floor in her column: a new Kernel read voice.say (workbench/voice_column.py) judges a goal's ways as field.either does, keeps their maths receipts, cuts each into voice_facts' fact sheet and says it through voice_gate.speak (cannot tell from the settle stage's receipt, so it carries where it holds and what keeps). Her column panel (mind_panel_qt) now says the proof's maths line in Why (matched to the line by its receipt) and each way in Either way through the floor, where 0.8.6's templates said them; the state word, the place in the proof and the receipt stay. With every 0.8.7 switch off, voice.say says it is off and the panel keeps 0.8.6's words exactly. Model words from a worded frame would come back as a stored model answer with the WORDED mark for model_marks_qt.place; her own words carry no mark. (2) Ask the Library is reachable: a tab 'Ask the Library' in the reference view, and from the writing line ('ask the library ...', 'library: ...', 'what does the library say about ...', any question while the reference view is in front, and an 'Ask the Library' link under her no-model card for a question). Her answer (workbench/library_qt.py) shows her lines in her order, the desk's own cut quote with the pointed words lit and the mark 'read by the model, checked against your desk' plus the fold for each ASK turn, the places as file · page · label with your words lit and why they matched (each opens its page in the reference view), the cross-references on wires, and the legal footer. (3) 'Read this table' in the reference view on a page the desk can cut a table from, with a 'Table' tab: the state as a word and a shape, her lines with the closing line in bold, then the columns, each role and who named it, and the rows. (4) Cross-references drawn on the page in the reference view: beside each place that refers to another, a quiet wire 'refers to § 12(a) · current'; beside the place referred to, 'referred to by § 12(b), § 12(c)'; a page opened from the Library scrolls to its place. (5) Leave it now runs the reads it says it runs (as the desk's deduction), and when none can run says 'cannot tell, because ...' instead of claiming reads; B5's Remember / Retire are shown on her cards in a real window; her clock's line 'Asking the model: 1 s of about 4 · Stop' sits under her card while a GOAL, READ or PICK turn runs, Stop reaches the turn, and the line goes when the turn ends. Found while wiring and fixed: her hand kept the live turn dict (with its thread and holder) in the session's her_plan, so the session could not be saved while a model turn ran (TypeError: Answer is not JSON serializable); and 'where ... came from' did not reach her hand from the writing line. Frames: 62, both looks at 1920x1200 and 1366x768, on Rail Demo and Home Demo built through their own doors in a throwaway folder, with the invented October statement from the exam papers brought in through intake.

decisions: Which switch governs her voice floor: the floor is no-model (C4), and the brief and design 2.12 say that with every 0.8.7 switch off she is exactly 0.8.6. So voice.say is on whenever any of the five switches is on (the defaults included) and off only when all five are off. The 'wording' switch keeps governing the model's FRAME turns, which W7 does not send.

Where the floor speaks: in her column panel's Why (the proof's maths line, found by its receipt, reasons._receipt over the same record) and Either way (each way, under the head of 0.8.6's sentence, as '<revision> applies: <her words>'). Rests on and What would settle it keep 0.8.6's words: they say what the answer rests on and who settles it, not the maths answer. 'Cannot tell, said well' comes through the same path for any way whose maths answer cannot tell (judged again at the settle stage for its zones and moves).
voice.say is a new read in a module of its own rather than a change to field.either: either_way drops the maths records from its answer, and 0.8.6's files stay as they are.

Labels for the fact sheet: each symbol's name from its row's parameter ('the rail voltage read 12 V'); the limit's owner from the way's revision ('Rev B's 4 W limit'). The design's 'the stopwatch read 45 ms' needs an instrument the desk does not record, so it reads 'the startup duration read 45 ms'.

The writing line goes to the Library only on words that ask it ('ask the library ...', 'library: ...', 'what does the library/my papers say about ...') or on a question while the reference view is in front; other questions keep their road, with a quiet 'Ask the Library' under the no-model card. Talk's questions are never taken.
In the reference view, Ask the Library asks the library chosen there (namespace); from her column it asks every library.

Leave it: B4's default takes only 'read' choices, and in her hand a desk reading is a navigation or a change, so in practice nothing is runnable there: Leave it now says 'cannot tell, because ...'. Where a read choice carries desk goals, they run with origin DEDUCED (the desk's default, not his choice).
Her clock's Stop sets the request's cancelled hook before the turn's thread starts, so turns.ask and the port's stream both see it.

To show the READ card, Remember and Retire in a real window, the smoke calls her hand's own B3 entry (read_words) for 'pull up where the bench numbers came from' with a reading of NONE, because on this desk 0.8.6's dictionary reads those words as four trace/select options and the writing line takes the GOAL card (whose clock line is the one in the frames).
